rationale: nodriver is a Python async browser automation library (v0.50.3) that communicates directly with Chromium-based browsers via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) over WebSocket, dropping Selenium and chromedriver binary dependencies. It is the stated successor to undetected-chromedriver with explicit focus on anti-bot evasion (CloudFlare, Captcha, Imperva, hCaptcha). The 77 Python files include 59 auto-generated CDP domain definitions; the remaining ~18 core modules implement browser launch, tab management, element interaction, and CDP message routing. The repo lacks any test suite, architecture/design documents, or JSON-LD extraction, script generation, self-healing, queue, fuzzy-matching, or fulltext-search capabilities. The AGPL-3.0 license may restrict commercial use. Tier B reflects direct relevance to the stealth and browser-automation pipeline concerns, moderate source size, and absence of tests or architectural depth.
limitations: No test files present; cannot verify stealth efficacy or automation correctness
No architecture/design documents beyond Sphinx scaffolding in docs/
AGPL-3.0 license requires source disclosure for network-deployed derivatives
59 of 77 .py files are auto-generated CDP bindings (via generate_cdp.py), not hand-written logic
Stealth claims (CloudFlare, Captcha bypass) are marketing statements in README/pyproject.toml; no implementation evidence cited in source
No JSON-LD extraction, script generation, self-healing selectors, queue/scheduling, fuzzy matching, or fulltext search functionality
Examples directory contains 7 scripts but no test harness
